errata.found_in: pass 2 (adversarial review), by reading the completed run's portfolio records against the code that produced the fields
errata.observed: The portfolio entry and the paste-able Note for the 'ridge' variant recorded the *selected node* policy (layer nodes, spacing 4) although deploy() had produced that file with spacing 1. Evidence: evidence/pindrop-v4-run1-report.json portfolio[1].policy = {layer: nodes, spacing: 4}; the file's own GeoTIFF tag said the same wrong thing, and its Note read 'dense ridge control k=4'.
errata.effect_on_pixels: None. Run 1's ridge field was built by deploy(deployed_raw, selected with layer=ridge, spacing=1); only the recorded policy, the raster tag and the Note were wrong.
errata.fix: The portfolio loop records {layer: ridge, spacing: 1} for the ridge variant. Re-runs 2 and 3 from the corrected source produced identical pixels, with the tag now reading 'ridge k=1 budget=0.0300 h=0 L=0'.
errata.prevention: gems3/pindrop_publish.check_variant_policies refuses any report whose recorded policy contradicts its variant (nodes must equal the frozen selection, the control must be a ridge spacing-1 policy at the selected budget and arm, discovery must be a distinct file with its own Note). Verified against the preserved run-1 report in tests/test_pindrop.py::test_publisher_refuses_a_report_whose_control_policy_contradicts_its_pixels. The publisher also prints the report path and hash it is publishing, and its default path is the published run.
errata.lesson: A control file is only a control if its own metadata says what it is. Reading the run record back against the export code caught it; pixel-level validation alone never could.

errata.found_in: pass 2, while comparing the reference table with the within-run comparison
errata.observed: Every earlier published file carried one generic caveat, although session 2 and session 3 published all-fold refits: every fold scored in this audit is in-sample for them, and the fusion files contain the SGMC traces the gap proxy is built from.
errata.fix: Per-file caveats now state in-sample status and SGMC circularity explicitly; the site renders them beside the reference table. The pre-registered primary comparison (nodes versus dense control, same arm, budget, folds) is unaffected and remains the only comparison this run treats as controlled.
errata.lesson: A high proxy number from an in-sample artifact is not evidence of superiority; a published file must be scored with its training footprint disclosed.

errata.found_in: pass 2, reading the run-2 Notes as a human would before pasting them into the competition form
errata.severity: cosmetic, user-visible in the submission form
errata.observed: The dense control's Note read 'dense ridge control dense s=3.000% ...' because the variant suffix and the shape text both carried the word 'dense'.
errata.fix: Shape text no longer repeats the layer word. Run 3, the published run, reads 'Pindrop v4 ridge | union-target HGB | dense ridge control s=3.000% h=0 L=0 | 4e03fc9705' (87 characters).
errata.lesson: The Note is the only part of a submission a human types; it was checked as rendered text, not only as a string that satisfies a length limit.

reproducibility.frozen_selection: identical in all three runs: union-target / nodes / spacing 4 / budget 0.0300 / halo 0 / tip 0
reproducibility.pixels: the nodes file and the dense control were pixel-identical in all three runs (0 differing pixels inside the template mask); the discovery file differed in 116 of its 155,021 emitted pixels between run 1 and runs 2-3, so that arm's retraining is not bit-reproducible
reproducibility.bytes: file hashes differ between runs; selection_sha256 hashes a frozen-selection record that contains its freeze timestamp, and run 2 to run 3 changed the reviewed policy/Note wording
reproducibility.cause_of_116_pixels: not established; the estimator is threaded and its audit known-DTI also moved by 1e-4 (0.1942 to 0.1941). No frozen decision changed.
